subject: Output entitlement playbook: MSA/order form redlines and implementation tie-ins
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@stellarlytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@stellarlytics.com
Date: 2026-10-25T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: StellarLytics redlines — MSA + Order Form (output use / training)

Karthik / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team attached redlines to the MSA and the order form focused on two areas we need clear controls on: (1) ownership/entitlement to model outputs and any downstream productization, and (2) explicit prohibition or opt‑in for training on StellarLytics data (including telemetry/feedback) — with auditability requirements.

High level asks:
- We need an assignment or exclusive-style right to outputs generated by models we send prompts to that are used to create our product content.
- No training on StellarLytics customer data without explicit written opt-in and notice, plus evidence of deletion or isolation.
- A small feedback license for diagnostics (anonymized) only, with retention limits.

I attached our redlines: Stellar_Redline_MSA.docx and Stellar_OrderForm_Redline.pdf. Can you confirm Redwood's willingness to accept constraints and propose workable language?

We'd like a short call with legal and product to align before procurement pushes this forward. Availability: next week afternoons PT.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Partnerships
StellarLytics

Attachments:
- Stellar_Redline_MSA.docx (redline)
- Stellar_OrderForm_Redline.pdf (redline)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@stellarlytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-25T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StellarLytics redlines — MSA + Order Form (output use / training)

Elena —

Appreciate the detailed redlines and the clear summary. I uploaded both docs to the deal record and looped in Laura (legal) and Ben (ops/technical). Quick plan:

1) Laura will review the legal asks and propose specific language for the MSA + Order Form.
2) Ben and I will confirm what we can commit to operationally (retention windows, telemetry isolation, audit exports).
3) We'll prepare a single consolidated redline from Redwood and propose a short legal/product call (30 minutes) next Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Two clarifying questions from my side to speed review:
- When you say "assignment or exclusive-style right to outputs", can you confirm if you mean: (a) assignment of rights in outputs generated by Redwood models when Stellar supplies the prompts and data (full assignment), or (b) a perpetual, exclusive license to use productized outputs? The solution space and implications differ.
- For training opt-in, do you require a per-deal explicit opt-in checkbox, or is a monthly written confirmation sufficient?

I'll wait for Laura's redline but wanted to confirm we received everything and to set expectations on timeline. Call availability: Tue 10/27 1:30–3:30pm PT or Wed 10/28 2:00–4:00pm PT.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-26T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StellarLytics redlines — MSA + Order Form (output use / training)

Karthik — quick operational notes for Laura to consider when drafting:

- Output ownership: We can support a commercial path for a customer to assert broad usage rights (including exclusive license), but assignment of IP on our hosted models has product/ops implications. Assignment on outputs generated from customer-provided prompts/data is more straightforward than assignment of model weights or derivatives of the base model. Recommend drafting around "exclusive/perpetual license to outputs generated using customer-provided prompts/data" rather than a blanket assignment.

- Training: We offer a "training opt-out" by default on hosted tier; opt-in can be a signed checkbox in the order form. For private deployments we can guarantee no training. For hosted, we can provide a documented process: (1) isolated dataset pipeline when opt-in, (2) retention windows, and (3) audit log export for training events.

- Feedback license: propose a scoped, non-exclusive diagnostic license limited to improving infrastructure and anonymized quality monitoring; retention 90 days unless agreed otherwise.

I'll pull examples of precedent language and baseline telemetry retention for the call.

Ben
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@stellarlytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: StellarLytics redlines — MSA + Order Form (output use / training)

Elena / Karthik —

Thanks for the redlines. I reviewed the attachments and Ben's operational notes and drafted a consolidated response with compromise language. Attached: Redwood_response_redline.docx and a short standalone proposed_sva_clause.txt for the order form. High-level positions we are prepared to offer:

1) Output entitlement: Redwood will grant StellarLytics a perpetual, worldwide, exclusive (with right to sublicense to end customers) license to outputs that are produced solely from prompts and data StellarLytics provides to the service and that are used by StellarLytics to create customer-facing product content. This does not extend to Redwood's underlying models or improvements to the model architecture.

2) Training & feedback:
   - Hosted offering: By default, StellarLytics will be opted out of being used to train Redwood models. An opt-in path can be added to the order form (checkbox). If opted in, training will be performed only after a signed addendum, using an isolated pipeline with documented provenance; Redwood will provide an audit export showing datasets used and retention dates.
   - Private deployment: No training on customer data unless explicitly agreed in writing.
   - Feedback license: Redwood requests a narrowly scoped, non-exclusive license limited to debugging, aggregated quality analysis, and safety monitoring. The license will be time-limited (90 days) for raw telemetry; derived, aggregated metrics may be retained longer for product improvement.

3) Evidence & audits: For enterprise customers, Redwood will provide an export of training activity and a certification of deletion for data used for training where applicable. We will propose a 30-day SLA for provisioning audit exports after a reasonable request.

4) Suggested order form language: see proposed_sva_clause.txt for the exact checkbox/opt-in text.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to confirm whether the exclusive license formulation above maps to Stellar's commercial needs (assignment vs exclusive license).
- If yes, we prepare consolidated redline and propose a 30‑minute legal + product call to finalize the order form checkbox and evidence workflow.

Attaching: Redwood_response_redline.docx (Redline), proposed_sva_clause.txt

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Redwood_response_redline.docx
- proposed_sva_clause.txt

Laura / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and concrete language. The exclusive license formulation looks acceptable to our commercial team; legal will do a final pass but I think we can avoid a full assignment requirement now. Two notes before the call:

- We'll ask for the audit export SLA to be included in the order form annex (30 days is acceptable).
- For hosted training opt-in, StellarLytics prefers the opt-in to be explicit at the order form level (checkbox) rather than per‑month confirmations.

We can take the call Tue 11/09 at 12:30pm PT — request meeting invite and draft consolidated redline in HubSpot before then.

Appreciate the pragmatic compromise.

Best,
Elena
Head of Partnerships, StellarLytics
